actions.description: Capture a single image from a named camera with a declared resolution and exposure and return an image artifact reference.

inputs.description: Select one declared image source; each capture is independent.
inputs.name: camera

actions.name: capture_image

actions.description: Capture a depth point cloud over a declared range and return a point-cloud artifact reference with the point count and coordinate frame.
actions.name: capture_point_cloud

facts.text: The launch file declares the default camera_name 'camera' and camera_namespace 'camera'.
README's default-behavior example lists node /camera/camera, topic /camera/camera/color/camera_info, and service /camera/camera/device_info.
README lists /camera/camera/color/camera_info and /camera/camera/color/metadata among the published topics of the default node.
The node constructs each stream's camera_info topic as ~/<stream_name>/camera_info.
The node creates a sensor_msgs::msg::CameraInfo publisher on that topic for non-SC streams.
The node creates the private ~/device_info service of type realsense2_camera_msgs::srv::DeviceInfo.
The DeviceInfo service response carries seven strings: device_name, serial_number, firmware_version, usb_type_descriptor, firmware_update_id, sensors and physical_port.
getDeviceInfo fills the response from the live device's name, serial number, firmware version, USB type descriptor, firmware update id, physical port and available ROS sensor names.
README documents device_info as retrieving the device serial number, firmware version and the other DeviceInfo fields.
The node constructs each stream's metadata topic as ~/<stream_name>/metadata and publishes realsense2_camera_msgs::msg::Metadata there.
realsense2_camera_msgs/msg/Metadata carries a std_msgs/Header and a json_data string.
README says the metadata messages store the camera's available metadata in JSON format.
handleHWReset stops every available ROS sensor and calls _dev.hardware_reset(); it catches exceptions and only warns, and its std_srvs/Empty response carries no failure status.
The launch file enables the color stream by default with the RGB8 color format.
The launch file enables the depth stream by default with the Z16 depth format; the infra, infra1 and infra2 streams default to false.
README's default topic list shows /camera/camera/color/image_raw, /camera/camera/depth/camera_info, /camera/camera/depth/image_rect_raw and /camera/camera/depth/metadata.
The node names each image topic ~/<stream_name>/image_raw, with image_rect_raw for the rectified depth stream.
The image publisher is a sensor_msgs::msg::Image publisher.
The node maps the Z16 format to the 16UC1 image encoding and RGB8 to rgb8.
Each image message gets the stream's optical frame id, the frame stamp, height, width, is_bigendian false and step = width * element size.
fix_depth_scale passes 16-bit depth samples through when the device depth scale is 0.001 m and otherwise rescales every sample to that unit.

Without stream intrinsics the node uses zeroed intrinsics; CameraInfo then gets the stream width, height and optical frame, K and P from fx, fy, ppx and ppy, an identity R and plumb_bob (5) or equidistant (4) distortion coefficients.
CameraInfo is stamped with the frame time and published only while it has subscribers.
Metadata JSON holds frame_number, clock_domain, frame_timestamp and every metadata key the frame supports; the message is published only while it has subscribers.
The launch file defaults pointcloud.enable to false, pointcloud.stream_filter to 2, pointcloud.ordered_pc to false and align_depth.enable to false.
README says the pointcloud filter adds the topic /camera/camera/depth/color/points.
The pointcloud filter creates its sensor_msgs::msg::PointCloud2 publisher on ~/depth/color/points only while it is enabled.
An unordered cloud gets width = valid point count, height 1 and is_dense true.
The launch file defaults enable_rgbd, enable_gyro, enable_accel and enable_motion to false.
IMU info is published once with the latched QoS profile, and the extrinsics publishers use the same latched profile.
The latched QoS profile is keep-last 1, reliable and transient-local.
